note:
Round 2 on the PDRN hero. Malcolm, 2026-08-24: 'the liquid inside the bottle is a transparent pink colored liquid (not white). And the skin of the model isnt good enough quality. you can see its not natural enough (AI detail distortions). Its subtle - but isnt quite good enough.'

HE IS RIGHT ABOUT THE SKIN, AND IT IS AN ENGINE PROBLEM, NOT A BRIEF PROBLEM. Zoomed to native pixels on the cheek beside the eye, the live frame carries a swirling fingerprint-like whorl pattern — concentric wavy micro-lines that follow no anatomical direction, closer to brain coral or crepe paper than to skin — plus an over-uniform sheen on the cheekbone. Compared across engines at the identical region, the artefact is present in nbp_flash, nbp_pro AND seedream, and absent from gpt-image, whose skin shows irregular pores, real freckles and lines running the natural directions of the face. Malcolm's own original pick was a gpt-image frame, which is why its skin read correctly to him in the first place.

THE ENGINE CONFLICT THAT MADE ROUND 1 CHOOSE BADLY. Round 1 assumed Nano Banana had to win because gpt-image caps at 2048px and the seven-line label needs pixels. That assumption was wrong and was never checked: PDRN-A-FAITHFUL-gpt_image_01 renders all seven lines correctly at 2048, because in this composition the bottle is 574px wide, which is a big enough budget. So there was never a trade between label and skin — I picked the engine on the label alone and shipped its skin. Round 2 corrects that: gpt-image is expected to win, and every supplier still runs per rule 1.

THE LIQUID, AND A CONFLICT WORTH SEEING BEFORE CHOOSING. The banner-library brief that produced Malcolm's frame stated the opposite of what he now wants: 'the serum is a CLEAR, COLOURLESS, WATER-TRANSPARENT liquid' and 'the glass colour is the colour of the GLASS ITSELF, not of the contents'. That instruction is what produced the solid, milky interior he is objecting to. He now wants a transparent PINK liquid. There are two ways to read that and they are not cosmetically equivalent, so both are generated:
  * L1-FROSTED keeps the frosted rose-pink glass of the product's own hero shot, and makes the interior read as a see-through pink fluid behind it, with the pipette stem visible and a meniscus at the fill line.
  * L2-CLEARGLASS makes the glass clear and puts the colour in the liquid, so the pink you see IS the serum.
L2 is the more literal reading of what Malcolm asked for, and it is the one that would NOT match the rest of the PDRN product photography, which shows frosted glass throughout. That is his call to make, not mine, which is why both go in front of him.

SKIN: NAMED, NOT WISHED FOR. The negatives name the specific artefact seen at 100% rather than asking vaguely for realism, and the positive side describes what real skin does — varied pore size, irregular spacing, lines in anatomical directions, real freckles at irregular intervals, vellus hair, and uneven sheen with matte and shiny areas. Per the lesson recorded in 'the brief caused the plainness', the negatives do not forbid texture itself, only the machine pattern.
